what_happened: Task 612's free-text description field is a verbatim, word-for-word duplicate of the description belonging to a separate, correctly-sited .dotfiles task (project_number 138, retire_machine_wide_sapience_surface, status not_started), narrating the SECOND-HALF machine-wide-removal work and asserting 'This task belongs in /home/benjamin/.dotfiles'. Task 612's own file_scope (agent-system/extensions/sapience/settings-fragment.json, manifest.json, EXTENSION.md, README.md, index-entries.json, two context/domain files, scripts/), title, project_name (gate_sapience_activation_behind_extension), and siting (specs dir under /home/benjamin/.config/nvim) all correctly identify it as the FIRST-HALF extension-side task. The description's own embedded ORDERING CONSTRAINT text is self-referentially paradoxical when read as task 612's own instructions (it calls itself 'the second half' depending on a companion of its own project name). This is a task-authoring/paste defect, not a real blocker in the underlying two-part change itself.

Found a complete, already-shipped precedent for the per-repo MCP-server-registration mechanism task 612 actually needs to build: the lean extension's install-lean-lsp-session-hook.sh + hooks/lean-lsp-register-project.sh + scripts/setup-lean-mcp.sh, which install a stable USER-LEVEL (never repo-local .claude/) SessionStart hook that detects per-project applicability and writes/repairs that project's own .projects[<path>].mcpServers entry in ~/.claude.json. Also confirmed via git diff that the extension settings-merge engine (lua/neotex/plugins/ai/shared/extensions/merge.lua) already fully supports merging a hooks object (SessionStart/PreToolUse/etc., with dedup and clean unmerge-on-unload) into a consuming repo's .claude/settings.local.json, not just permissions.allow -- so the 5 Sapience hooks and 7 read-tool grants can both move into settings-fragment.json using an already-proven mechanism; only the ~/.claude.json mcpServers piece needs the lean-lsp-style stable-path hook+writer pattern.
